title: 10-minute LLM smoke lab and handoff kit
content:
Goal:
- Provide a reproducible 10-minute lab that a product engineer or integrator can run locally to validate an SDK integration and produce the artifacts needed for an internal handoff (telemetry, sample traces, and a simple regression prompt).

Audience:
- New SDK adopters (engineers), solutions engineers doing PoCs, and internal reviewers (SRE / infra).

Why this exists:
- We want a short, observable, low-friction path that proves the critical pieces: auth, streaming fallback, retry semantics, and telemetry contracts. This is intentionally compact: not a full production checklist but a fast confidence builder you can run during a demo or kickoff.

Prerequisites (3 min):
1) Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ installed.
2) Checkout the local sdk-stub repo or use the hosted sandbox endpoint. Quick clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-stub.git && cd sdk-stub && npm ci
3) A Redwood API key with "sandbox" scope (or set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var).
4) Docker available if you want the hermetic stub run (optional).

Success criteria (observable):
- SDK makes a successful streaming call and receives at least one "token" chunk within 500ms of request start (simulated environment).
- Telemetry emits a request.timing span and a model.selection tag.
- A trace ID appears in the console and in the telemetry debug logs.
- A regression prompt returns the previously seen canonical output (or flags a quality drift).

Lab steps (10 minutes):
Step 0 (0:30) - Pick mode: local stub or hosted sandbox\- Local stub: ./scripts/start-stub.sh (starts a tiny HTTP server that mimics Redwood API; binds to http://localhost:8080)\- Hosted sandbox: export REDWOOD_API_BASE=https://sandbox.redwood.ai

Step 1 (1:00) - Quick smoke script (Node example)\- Create a file quick-smoke.js with the snippet below and run node quick-smoke.js. Expect streaming tokens printed to console and an appended trace-id.\nconst Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');\nconst client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_API_BASE || 'http://localhost:8080' });\n(async () => {\n  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rwd-small-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize: why we built Redwood.' }] });\n  let firstChunkTime = Date.now();\n  for await (const chunk of stream) {\n    process.stdout.write(chunk.text);\n  }\n  console.log('
TRACE_ID=' + stream.traceId);\n})();

Expected quick outcomes:
- Console shows tokens within 300–700ms.
- Final line contains TRACE_ID=...

Step 2 (2:00) - Validate telemetry contract\- Using the local stub, tail the telemetry debug log: tail -f logs/telemetry-debug.log\- Confirm you see lines like: request.start id=TRACE_ID, request.timing duration_ms=XX, model.selection=rwd-small-1\- If using hosted sandbox, open the dev console (link in linked_artifacts) and search trace id.

Step 3 (2:30) - Exercise failure and retry semantics\- Cause a transient 503 from the stub: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/_simulate -d '{"mode":"503-once"}'\- Re-run the quick-smoke.js. Expect the SDK to retry once and succeed. Confirm telemetry: span.retry_count=1 and a retry.reason=503 in logs.

Step 4 (1:00) - Latency and batching probe\- Run three concurrent clients: node quick-smoke.js & node quick-smoke.js & node quick-smoke.js\- Observe server logs: batch.size should be 3 for the server-side aggregation simulation. If not, note environment variable BATCH_WINDOW_MS in the stub config.

Step 5 (1:00) - Regression prompt check\- Run node quick-smoke.js with the canonical prompt: 'List three reasons Redwood optimizes inference for production.'\- Save output to smoke-output.txt and compare to golden-output.txt (included in repo). If diffs exist, file an issue with tag sdk-smoke-regression and include TRACE_ID.

Handoff artifact checklist (what to attach to a handoff ticket):
- smoke-output.txt (actual output)
- golden-output.txt (expected)
- TRACE_ID from the run
- telemetry-debug.log excerpt (10–30 lines around request.start and request.end)
- short note: environment used (local stub vs hosted sandbox) and node/python version

Common failure modes + quick fixes:
- No tokens streamed: "auth failed" -> verify REDWOOD_API_KEY; run curl ${REDWOOD_API_BASE:-http://localhost:8080}/v1/health
- Telemetry missing: stub not started with telemetry enabled -> start with TELEMETRY=1 ./scripts/start-stub.sh
- Retry didn't happen: SDK configured with retries=0 in local config -> check ~/.redwoodrc or SDK init options
- Batch size always 1: BATCH_WINDOW_MS set to 0 in stub -> bump to 50ms for visible batching during lab

Additional experiments (optional, +5–10 minutes):
- Token-level cost: run the same prompt at model=rwd-medium-quant and compare token count / simulated cost in telemetry.log\- Canary failover: simulate a region outage (./scripts/start-stub.sh --region us-east simulate-down) and confirm automatic fallback to us-west endpoint and a model.variant tag in telemetry

Mini-FAQ (for engineers doing the handoff):
Q: How do I reproduce the streaming behavior in CI?
A: Use the hermetic docker image (./ci/start-hermetic-stub.sh) which emits identical traces. CI should store TRACE_ID and upload telemetry snippet as artifact.

Q: How do I capture the trace in Datadog / Honeycomb?
A: Include the span.exporter env var pointing to the test exporter in stub config. See linked_artifacts confluence page for exporter snippets.

Q: Who to ping for a blocked telemetry schema mismatch?
A: @Leila Morgan (obs team) and @Samir Bhatt (devexp) — include example payload and trace id.

Next steps after a successful run:
- Create a short ticket in ENG-BOARD with attachments above and tag eng-serving-runtime + eng-observability.
- For customers: if this was a PoC, capture a short video (30–60s) of the console run and upload to the customer folder.

Notes to self (authoring hints):
- Keep the quick-smoke script intentionally tiny; we want a single collapse-and-run action.
- Maintain golden-output.txt alongside the stub repo and periodically rebaseline on major model onboarding.
- Consider a one-click GitHub Action that runs the smoke lab and posts TRACE_ID to PR comments.

Revision log:
- 2025-02-26 initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-03-04 added retry and batching simulation notes (Leila)

Quick links (local):
- repo: ./sdk-stub/
- golden outputs: ./sdk-stub/golden/golden-output.txt
- start script: ./sdk-stub/scripts/start-stub.sh

If anything is unclear or flaky during the run, paste the TRACE_ID into the #devexp channel and tag one of us.
